content.title: About
content.content: High‑protein toasted bread is a whole‑grain loaf enriched with plant‑based or whey protein. After toasting it develops a crunchy crust while staying soft inside, offering a rich, nutty aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Athletes and diet‑conscious people often choose high‑protein bread to boost daily protein intake.
Toasting intensifies flavor and crunch without significantly reducing nutrients.
Recipes may include sunflower, pumpkin or flax seeds, further increasing protein and healthy fat content.
This bread typically has a lower glycemic index than regular white bread.
Manufacturers use a slow‑mixing dough process to improve gluten structure and retain more protein.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Each slice provides about 10–12 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and post‑workout recovery.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: The whole‑grain base supplies fiber that aids digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Toasted bread raises blood sugar more slowly, which is beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 vitamins help with energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc support muscle function and immune health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of added protein and seeds, a slice can contain up to 250 kcal; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you have hypertension.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Certain recipes use artificial sweeteners or preservatives; check the label if you avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted high‑protein bread works well for sandwiches with lean meat, cottage cheese, avocado or hummus. Use it as a base for open‑face toast, a side for soups, or simply as a crunchy snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze individual slices and re‑toast before eating.
